overall_summary: Bitcoin is digesting a sharp crash-and-rebound amid heavy ETF outflows and historic deleveraging, while large off-exchange pulls offer some support. Macro signals are mixed with soft-dollar hints against still-high Fed hike odds and key PCE data ahead. Geopolitical escalations add a risk-off overlay, leaving the near-term path unresolved.
key_points: ETF outflows continue; large BTC pulled off exchanges
Historic Binance deleveraging after $55K crash rebound
Dollar softens but December hike odds stay elevated
Core PCE and GDP data loom as next catalysts
Geopolitical tensions rise across Ukraine, Iran, Libya

items.title: Bitcoin crashes to $55K two-year low then rebounds above $61K
items.summary: Bitcoin plunged as low as about fifty-five thousand dollars over the weekend, its weakest level since September twenty twenty-four, amid a brutal AI and tech stock sell-off plus roughly one point eight billion dollars in crypto liquidations. It has clawed back above sixty-one thousand on Monday as Nasdaq futures bounced hard. Traders should watch whether this bounce holds when Wall Street fully opens and ahead of Wednesday PCE data, because the move was driven more by forced short covering and equity correlation than fresh spot demand. Extreme fear readings and the washout leave the market fragile either way.
items.impact: Sets near-term range and volatility around key levels with equity beta still high

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs bleed another $1.8B last week
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about six hundred sixty-nine million dollars in outflows on Friday alone, the biggest single day since June, pushing last week's total near one point eight billion and November's tally past four billion. BlackRock's IBIT drove the bulk of the redemptions. Persistent structural outflows signal institutions are still reducing exposure amid rate-hike fears, so any price recovery needs to overcome this headwind rather than lean on ETF demand.
items.impact: Removes a key bid and keeps downside pressure if redemptions continue

items.title: Abraxas Capital pulls over $1B Bitcoin off exchanges
items.summary: On-chain trackers flagged Abraxas Capital withdrawing roughly seventeen thousand six hundred BTC, worth about one billion dollars, from Binance and Kraken during the dip below sixty thousand at an average near fifty-nine thousand. The move looks like accumulation or custody transfer into cold storage right as liquidations peaked. Large exchange outflows of this size often reduce immediate sell pressure and can mark smart-money buying, giving traders a signal that some big players viewed the flush as an opportunity.
items.impact: Supports the bounce by locking up supply and signaling institutional dip-buying

items.title: Kraken CAD books crash Bitcoin to $17K equivalent; trades stand
items.summary: Kraken's Canadian-dollar order books decoupled overnight, sending BTC slash CAD as low as twenty-four thousand two hundred fifty Canadian dollars, roughly seventeen thousand US, while the rest of the market traded near fifty-five to fifty-eight thousand. Ether, XRP and even USD slash CAD were hit similarly. Kraken confirmed no breach and that all executed trades stand, so lucky buyers keep the discount and sellers eat the loss. This highlights thin-liquidity and market-maker risk on specific pairs even when global prices hold.
items.impact: Exchange-specific event with limited systemic price effect but raises venue risk awareness

items.title: South Korea expands crypto account freezes and transfer curbs
items.summary: South Korea's financial regulator announced plans to broaden powers to freeze crypto accounts beyond phishing cases to other serious financial crimes and to tighten scrutiny of transfers to overseas exchanges and private wallets. The existing phishing freeze system has already hit more than eleven thousand five hundred accounts. A comprehensive crypto legal framework draft is also expected this week. Tighter rules in a major Asian market can slow flows and raise compliance costs for local traders and platforms.
items.impact: Adds regulatory overhang that may reduce regional liquidity and risk appetite

items.title: Binance BTC open interest drops nearly 40% in historic deleveraging
items.summary: Bitcoin open interest on Binance has fallen nearly forty percent over the past year, about four and a half billion dollars, marking the largest dollar deleveraging on record according to CryptoQuant data. Recent weekend liquidations accelerated the unwind after months of high monthly wipeouts. Heavy leverage flush leaves the market cleaner with less crowded positioning, which can reduce cascade risk on the next move but also means less fuel for sharp rallies until fresh capital returns.
items.impact: Cleans positioning and lowers immediate liquidation cascade risk while muting upside volatility

items.title: Bessent Warns Fed Risks Overtightening After Market Rout
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that the Federal Reserve could be making a policy mistake by overtightening in response to recent inflation data, noting substantial tightening in financial conditions and signs of fragility after the equity selloff. This comes as some Fed officials have floated a possible half-point December hike. Crypto traders should care because administration pushback can temper hawkish expectations and support risk assets if it leads to a milder policy path.
items.impact: Eases aggressive hike bets, potential tailwind for Bitcoin and risk markets

items.title: Dollar Retreats from 19-Month High as Hike Odds Soften
items.summary: The US dollar index eased off its strongest levels since April 2025, trading around 103.6 to 103.8, as traders fully priced out a 50-basis-point December hike and left roughly 93 to 96 percent odds of a standard 25-basis-point move. The pullback followed last week's risk-asset rout and Bessent's comments. A softer dollar typically improves global liquidity conditions and has historically been supportive for Bitcoin.
items.impact: Weaker DXY provides relief for crypto and risk assets

items.title: Treasury Yields Rebound as Futures Rise Ahead of Williams
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed about 4 basis points to near 4.96 percent and the 2-year rose more sharply on Monday as US stock futures bounced hard after last week's sharp AI and tech-led correction. Markets are awaiting New York Fed President John Williams' remarks later today on the outlook and policy. Yield moves matter for crypto because higher rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets and can pressure valuations across risk markets.
items.impact: Yield volatility and Williams speech set near-term rate tone

items.title: Wednesday Core PCE and GDP Second Estimate Take Center Stage
items.summary: The key data this week arrives Wednesday with October Core PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, expected around 0.3 percent month-over-month and roughly 3.2 percent year-over-year, alongside the second estimate of third-quarter GDP near 3.4 percent. After recent sticky inflation prints and hawkish Fed commentary, these numbers will heavily influence December rate expectations. Crypto traders watch this closely as a hot print would reinforce higher-for-longer while a cooler one could fuel a broader risk rebound into the holiday-shortened week.
items.impact: High-volatility catalyst for rates, dollar, and Bitcoin direction

items.title: German Flash PMI Hits Multi-Year High, UK Softens
items.summary: Germany's S&P Global flash composite PMI surged to 55.0 in November, the strongest since early 2022, with manufacturing at a 56-month high of 55.0 and services at 54.0, both beating forecasts and signaling a broadening recovery. The UK composite eased to 52.3 with services weaker. Stronger European growth data reduces global recession fears and supports the risk-on narrative that can lift Bitcoin, though the US flash PMIs due today remain the more immediate focus.
items.impact: Positive global growth signal supportive for risk assets

items.title: December 25bp Fed Hike Odds Hold Firm Near 95 Percent
items.summary: Despite the equity rout, Bessent's warning, and pared aggressive bets, CME FedWatch still shows around 96 percent probability of a quarter-point rate increase at the December 8-9 meeting. Hawkish recent Fed speak and elevated inflation readings keep the base case intact even as 50-basis-point odds have vanished. This higher-for-longer backdrop remains a headwind for Bitcoin until the PCE data or Williams speech shifts the narrative.
items.impact: Sustains rate pressure and USD support against crypto upside

items.title: Ukraine sinks Russian warship with drones in Libya
items.summary: President Zelensky confirmed Ukraine used seven naval drones to sink the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi port and hit a weapons-linked cargo ship. The attack expands the war far beyond the Black Sea into North Africa and hits one of Russia's newer vessels. Traders should watch for Russian retaliation, higher shipping risk premiums, and any knock-on to Mediterranean energy routes.
items.impact: Heightens geopolitical risk premium and risk-off pressure on crypto and equities

items.title: Iran vows all tools against US blockade as Trump eyes strikes
items.summary: Iran's foreign ministry said it will use every available means to confront the US naval blockade, calling it military aggression, a day after Trump threatened to sink any Iranian tankers that try to break it and signaled possible renewed strikes after New Year if no deal. The standoff keeps Strait of Hormuz risk elevated and oil prices sensitive. Crypto traders care because another escalation spike in energy costs fuels inflation fears and tighter financial conditions.
items.impact: Sustains oil risk premium and broader risk-asset volatility

items.title: Libya pipeline shutdown cuts 350,000 barrels a day
items.summary: Libya's National Oil Corporation said an outlaw group shut a valve on the pipeline from the giant Sharara field, slashing output by about 350,000 barrels per day on top of an existing smaller outage. Combined losses near 365,000 bpd remove a meaningful chunk of supply while Middle East tensions already keep markets tight. Higher oil prices from this kind of disruption typically pressure risk assets including Bitcoin through the inflation and rates channel.
items.impact: Tightens oil supply and supports higher energy prices

items.title: COP31 climate talks collapse without fossil fuel deal
items.summary: The UN climate summit in Turkey ended without a final agreement after the EU and others rejected a text that omitted any clear commitment on fossil fuels, making it one of the rare full collapses of the process. Talks ran deep into overtime but exposed deep splits between oil producers and ambition-focused nations. For markets the near-term effect is limited, though it leaves longer-term energy transition policy more uncertain and can support fossil fuel sentiment at the margin.
items.impact: Policy uncertainty for energy transition; limited immediate market move

items.title: NATO meets after Russian missiles enter Polish airspace
items.summary: NATO's North Atlantic Council gathers in Brussels today after Russian cruise missiles and a drone crossed into Poland during a large attack on Ukraine, with Secretary General Rutte pledging to defend every inch of Polish territory. The incident follows a Ukrainian drone hit on a sanctioned Russian cargo ship near Finland that drifted into Finnish waters. Any concrete NATO force enhancements or sharper rhetoric raise the odds of wider European escalation that markets hate.
items.impact: Raises NATO-Russia confrontation risk and defensive risk-off flows

items.title: Russian strikes kill 15 in Kyiv region apartment collapse
items.summary: Russian drone and missile attacks killed at least 15 people in the Kyiv region, including after a strike partially collapsed a five-story apartment block in Dymer where rescuers are still searching rubble. The intensified winter barrage also hit energy and civilian targets as temperatures drop. Persistent high-intensity fighting keeps Ukrainian and European risk elevated and can weigh on broader risk appetite when combined with other flashpoints.
items.impact: Sustains Ukraine war intensity and regional risk premium
